Files with no environment variable read or set: doc/tree-vis/Makefile, packaging/positron-dice/postinst, packaging/positron-dice/postrm, packaging/positron-dice/prerm, packaging/postinst, packaging/preinst, packaging/prerm, packaging/tron-host/preinst.in (its @TRON_HOST_REQUIRED_CPU_FLAGS@ is filled in by CMake, not by the environment), rust/run-cargo-test-binary, t/proxy/ctest-trampoline.sh. Names seen and left out on purpose: (1) SELF_DIR at perfetto/launcher-common:7 uses the ${NAME:?} form, but perfetto/tronperf:3 and perfetto/wrapper:3 assign it before they source the file, and nothing exports it. It is a shell variable passed from a script to the file it sources. An environment value never takes effect through the two launchers. (2) TRON_TRACE_FROM_TOKEN appears only in the usage text of perfetto/tronperf (lines 53-65). tronperf does not read or set it. runtron inherits it. (3) TORCH_LOGS appears only in a commented-out line (ingest/build-all.sh:55). (4) OMP_THREAD_LIMIT appears only in the comment at GNUmakefile:93-94, which says that the nproc command honors it. See the notes of NPROC_BUILD. (5) TMPDIR is not named in any file. mktemp reads it at perfetto/launcher-common:177, 182 and 314, perfetto/tools/rinzler-capture.sh:309, rust/run-cargo-test-binary:28, rust/rust-toolchain.sh:219 and packaging/tron-host/build-deb.sh:71. (6) Make built-in names that the environment does not supply in normal use: MAKE, CURDIR, MAKEOVERRIDES, MAKEFILE_LIST. (7) Make variables that the GNUmakefile assigns with ':=' on every path (for example RUN, BUILD_TYPE, DEB_VERSION, CMAKE_PRESET): the environment cannot change them. Only the make command line can. Make semantics used for the classification, checked with scratch makefiles on GNU Make 4.3 (outside the checkout): 'NAME ?= value' keeps an environment value even when it is empty. 'NAME := value' wins over the environment. 'ifndef NAME' treats an empty environment value as undefined. $(origin NAME) is 'environment' for an empty environment value. Two entries, HAS_AVX512 and TRON_INGEST_PLUGIN_BUNDLE_STAMP_REQUIRED, are internal make variables that the environment can supply only on the paths where the makefile does not assign them. They have confidence medium and may belong in a separate 'unintended inputs' list. REMOVE_GLOBAL, USER_INSTALL and VERBOSE in rust/rust-toolchain.sh are shell variables that the script tests without first giving them a value, so the environment supplies them. REMOVE_GLOBAL can lead to 'apt-get remove' of Rust packages when the script runs as root. Inside the block GNUmakefile:266-363, which is skipped when the only goals are list-tests or list-tests-core, the makefile defines ENABLE_FUSE_STATS and several internal variables (FUSE_STATS_STAMP, PRESET_STAMP, SCRATCH_DIRS). For those two goals nothing uses them. The 'when' value 'each run of the script' is also used for make, where it means each make run. Audience choices that another area may refine: TRON_HW_SAMPLER, TRON_TRACE_CATEGORIES and TRACE_FILE are product variables whose product readers are outside this area. TRON_TOKENIZE_PY is also read by rinzler.
